what: The Debt Tracker is a simple IOU ledger for money you lend and borrow. Each entry records a person, an amount, the date and a note, and the tracker keeps a running balance for everyone, so you always know who owes you and whom you owe.
It works like a paper khata or credit notebook used by families and small shops around the world, but with search, statements, CSV export and WhatsApp reminders.
Your ledger is private: it is stored only in this browser on this device and never uploaded. Download a backup file regularly so you never lose it.
uses: Remember every amount and when it was repaid.
Track customers who buy now and pay later.
Record who covered what over time.
Keep track of money you need to pay back.
Send a clear statement or a polite reminder.
tutorial: Your data stays in this browser only. Plan to download a backup now and then.
Tap “I gave / lent money” when money leaves you, or “I got / borrowed money” when you receive it.
Type the person’s name (earlier names are suggested), the amount, the date and an optional note, then press Add entry or Enter.
The tiles show what others owe you, what you owe and the net. Each person card shows their balance.
Tap a person to see only their entries. Press Send reminder to open WhatsApp with a friendly message.
Search notes or names. Use × to delete a wrong entry.
Use Statement PDF, Export CSV or Download backup. Restore backup loads a backup file.
features: Owes you, you owe or settled.
Stored only on your device, never uploaded.
For everyone or one person, with a running balance.
Open in Excel or Google Sheets.
Move your ledger between devices with a file.
A polite message with the balance.
Find entries by name or note.

example.title: Worked example: lending to a friend
example.text: You lend Sam 1,200.50 on 1 March and he repays 200 on 15 March. You also borrow 75 from Lena. Sam’s card shows “Owes you 1,000.50”, Lena’s shows “You owe 75.00”, and the tiles show others owe you 1,000.50, you owe 75.00 and the net is 925.50.

tips: Add entries right away, with a short note like “bus fare” or “repaid in cash”.
Download a backup every week or month and keep it in a safe place.
Share a statement PDF before asking for repayment so there is no confusion.
Use the same spelling for each name so entries stay together.
problems: The ledger lives in this browser. Private browsing, clearing site data or a different browser shows an empty ledger. Restore your latest backup.
Restore says it is not a backup
Choose the .json file made by Download backup, not a CSV.
Names are matched without regard to capital letters, but spelling must match. Delete the wrong entries and add them again with the right name.
